scope: Cloud source and focused isolated verification for the Fabric Tencent resources window only. The Tencent dispatcher was exercised through fake and in-process provider adapters; no Tencent API was called, no instance was deployed, no production network was reached, no real charge, purchase or deletion ran, and no candidate or release was published.

implemented.name: Provider-neutral resource dispatch surface
implemented.change: The coordination Service now dispatches through a ResourceDispatcher interface (Provider()/EnsureResources) instead of the Local-only LocalResourceDispatcher/EnsureLocal pair. NewResourceIntent/ResourceResult/NetworkFact and validResourceResult replace the previous Local-named types, and read.go reads the provider-neutral result. cmd/fabric/main.go builds the dispatcher from the process's actual provider: local-docker -> NewLocalDispatcher, tencent-tke -> NewTencentDispatcher, both only when a coordination database is configured. Start now takes exactly one dispatcher argument.

implemented.name: Accepted Tencent resource plan resolution and tenant-account binding
implemented.change: TencentProvider.ResolveAcceptedResourcePlan maps one accepted Catalog ResourcePlanSnapshot back to this deployment's single provider profile entry: it requires provider/providerProfileId 'tencent-tke', BillingMode PREPAID_MONTHLY, prepaidMonths>0, the configured region, and an exact SKU/CPU/memory/capacity/period/renew match against a profile package, and it must not be ambiguous. The tenant is resolved to a provider account through a new explicit profile accountBindings list; a missing or duplicated tenant binding is rejected (tencent_account_binding_required/_ambiguous) before any capacity check or mutation. Binding decode rejects empty/duplicate tenants.

implemented.name: Tencent resource orchestration with prepaid readback and network fact
implemented.change: NewTencentDispatcher runs read-only prepaid monthly preflight (compute and storage) before any mutation, then drives CreateComputeAllocation -> GetComputeAllocation poll -> provider ReadComputeAllocation, CreateStorageVolume -> ReadStorageVolume, CreateStorageAttachment -> ReadStorageAttachment. Every readback is validated against the original intent: exact compute/storage IDs, account, workspace, PREPAID chargeType, NOTIFY_AND_MANUAL_RENEW renewFlag, non-empty prepaid deadline, ins-/disk-/pv- provider references, matching zone/region and package. It returns a NetworkFact of tke-node-pool/<pool> plus zone/region from the provider readback. An unconfirmed state returns errResourceDispatchPending (unknown, never absent) and never reports success. Application deployment is not reachable: no CreateWorkspaceRuntime call exists in the path, and the fake provider's runtime methods fail the test if reached.

implemented.name: Durable resume: funded dispatch, replayed identity, no re-purchase
implemented.change: resume dispatches through the configured provider only after the owning funding evidence for that provider's approved billing mode is verified, under a workspace advisory lock that re-reads the original operation status. Every attempt reuses the original committed resource IDs, provider keys and operation, so a lost response or restart replays the same purchase and readback instead of minting a second one. On success it persists the original provider effect identity (fabric.resource_actions.approved_input->resourceEffectIdentity) with compute/storage/attachment/network provider references and request ids, records the funding evidence, derives the network fact row by deterministic id (ON CONFLICT), sets provider_expires_at from the provider prepaid deadline, and confirms the resource set. readResourceResult supplies the execution binding Serve reads; a confirmed replay never dispatches again.

fundingVerification.localDocker: Verified through Ledger.ReadLocalNoChargeReceipt (owner readback), unchanged behavior: receipt id/owner/kind/outcome/operation and quote/commit evidence must all match the original command.
fundingVerification.tencentPrepaidMonthly: Fabric re-reads the exact confirmed wallet charge through LedgerCoordination.ReadReceiptByReference(owner=workspace, ownerEvidenceReference=obligationId) and requires receipt owner workspace, operationId == obligationId, kind WALLET_ACTION, outcome CONFIRMED, and id == ConfirmedChargeReceiptId. When the owner does not return that exact confirmed charge the intent stays unknown and no provider mutation runs. The owner-read receipt is persisted as fundingEvidence {source: ledger_confirmed_wallet_charge, receipt}.

focusedAuthorizationChain.note: The Tencent resource path is a strict PREPAID monthly purchase chain. Nothing below purchases, renews, refunds or deletes a resource.
steps: Workspace accepted an exact Catalog quote and created the funded obligation (TKE B window).
Workspace submits EnsureResources with the frozen ResourcePlanSnapshot and confirmedChargeReceiptId.
Fabric re-reads the accepted quote from Catalog and, for Tencent, re-reads the confirmed wallet charge from Ledger.
Only then does Fabric resolve the provider package and tenant account, run prepaid preflight, and drive the provider create/readback under the original operation keys.

commands.detail: coordination (PostgreSQL-backed, includes TestTencentPrepaidResourcesConfirmOnlyWithVerifiedOwnerFunding, TestTencentDispatcher* and TestResourceAcceptanceAndReadback), internal/fabric (accepted-plan resolver tests) and cmd/fabric all pass. Without OPL_OWNER_MIGRATION_TEST_ADMIN_DSN the three PostgreSQL-backed coordination tests (TestProcessServesAcceptedResourcesAndOwnerOperation, TestResourceAcceptanceAndReadback, TestTencentPrepaidResourcesConfirmOnlyWithVerifiedOwnerFunding) self-skip; the Tencent dispatcher unit tests run either way.

verificationBoundaries: All Tencent coverage uses fake or in-process provider adapters; no live Tencent API, CVM/CBS purchase, renewal or deletion was performed.
No instance was deployed, no protected production network was reached, and no candidate or release was produced.

The old Fabric TKE application writer (CreateWorkspaceRuntime and its HTTP routes) is deliberately retained: it may only be retired once Serve takes over the real caller and its obligations are verified. This window did not remove or change it.

sharedContractGaps.problem: Fabric verifies a Tencent prepaid charge only through LedgerCoordination.ReadReceiptByReference, whose server handler (services/ledger/eventconsumer/coordination.go) delegates to ReadLocalNoChargeReceipt and therefore serves only local_no_charge receipts: it rejects with not-found for a wallet-action receipt. The Tencent funding gate in services/fabric/coordination/resume.go reads kind WALLET_ACTION through that same RPC, so against the current Ledger implementation it can never return owner evidence and a Tencent intent would stay unknown forever.
sharedContractGaps.exactChange: Give Fabric one owner-verifiable read of the confirmed prepaid charge by obligation: either extend ReadReceiptByReference (or a new Ledger RPC) so a wallet-action receipt is returned for owner=workspace with ownerEvidenceReference=obligationId, or provide the confirmed charge through an equivalent owner readback Fabric may call. consumer = services/fabric/coordination/resume.go readConfirmedWalletCharge; field needed = id/owner/operationId/kind/outcome of the confirmed wallet-action charge (plus amount/obligation if the owner exposes them).
sharedContractGaps.rejectionCases: missing receipt; receipt for another obligation; wrong kind; UNCONFIRMED/REJECTED outcome; id not equal to ConfirmedChargeReceiptId - all must remain unknown and dispatch nothing.
sharedContractGaps.note: This window implemented the honest, contract-shaped owner readback rather than trusting an unverified reference; the local_no_charge path is unaffected.

claimBoundary: This receipt claims Cloud source changes in services/fabric and an isolated in-process focused test across the coordination, internal/fabric and cmd/fabric packages. It does not claim a deployable Tencent chain, an instance deployment, a candidate, a release, or any charge, purchase, renewal or deletion. The shared contract gap above is an explicit coordinator obligation.
secrets: none: the receipt contains no credentials, tokens, keys, customer data or private addresses; the isolated test database is a loopback container created for this run.
